topic: Galactic Structure and Cross-Scale K-Field Geometry
audience: High-school seniors; first-principles teaching, with concrete prerequisite capabilities and taught bridges.
prerequisites: Signed arithmetic, fractions, ratios, powers, linear equations, and coordinate graphs
learning_outcomes: Separate a position direction from an unoriented galaxy axis
Trace a source-defined response into an address system
Read its basis, units, handedness, and origin
Compare galaxy and Cell3 constructions without identifying their physical normals
Reconstruct distance from a small positive metric
Track occupancy across levels without discarding sparse or weak regions
Explain a frozen comparison and retain phase drifts and mismatches
Compare recurring structures by explicit transformations and independent predictions
requested_deliverables: capstone.md with full answers and rubric
assumptions: A topical short course, not a semester per topic. Pacing is 55-minute core lessons plus capstone periods; split dense lessons if actual learner load requires it.
No prior calculus, abstract algebra, university linear algebra, or quantum mechanics unless explicitly taught earlier.
Required core assessments must be solvable with taught finite examples. Clearly label deeper recognition-only extensions.
Markdown is the delivery format; no PDF or Word generation is required.

Read-only sources: no source-data copies, database exports, reindexing, or large arrays. Persist only authored course artifacts, compact provenance, audits, and small clearly synthetic examples.
Cell3 uses ICRS columns [a b c], an intentional negative determinant, and half-open cells [-1/2,1/2)^3. Use x-O_K in affine reciprocal identities.
Use the mature locked geometry and exact source provenance. Historical and corrected numerical branches remain separately labeled; do not silently mix their constants.
Use M_cell=B^T B and R_cell=M_cell^-1; distinguish G_phase, G_eff, reciprocal bases, distance Q, Q_g, and Q_nu.
Gauge-carrier tuples use color-first C_3 direct-sum W_2. A weak-first view needs an explicit permutation.
Do not merge detector parity, A1 carry parity, projective signs, chirality, family labels, primitive lifts, or distinct dyadic and ternary recursions.
Declare nearest-integer half-ties and the corresponding residual interval consistently; the half-open cell ownership rule is a separate operation.
The detail-product identity needs explicit hypotheses on E beyond Q=I-E; retain the product of finite differences.
M19 contains mixed extension branches and is not a premise of M20 core closure. Reconstruct prerequisites from module requires, with the documented audit corrections.

Preserve mature-source claims and accepted integration dispositions separately. In the integration only compiler M03, M07, M08 have direct authority; these compiler labels are not automatically the mathematical-backbone module labels. Preserve the admitted global-form family Z1,Z2,Z3,Z6 and source-local uniqueness claims with explicit contracts.
Treat matching dimensions or graph labels as neither an intertwiner nor a proof. A missing proof body remains a source-reported status with a retrieval gap.

Physical CMB velocity is distinct from phase-transformed vectors; the testbench admitted speed is 369812.50200040644 m/s. The Galactic Center is a visual gauge; do not invent Solar or Galactic short-window dynamics.
A photon-equivalent model energy is not measured transferred energy, and phase is not force. Preserve signed events and the three independent plane-cost levels in the fourteen-row 2026-08-26 bundle.
Cell3 and galaxy-derived cells have separately typed units, metrics, handedness, scales, and normals. Recurrence is an explanatory target, not permission to merge definitions.
Every residual remains a primary coordinate. Transformations are reversible or accompanied by all removed components and reconstruction rules; no outlier deletion or significance-based erasure.

course_map.title: Sky positions and projective axes
course_map.worked_example_capability: Separate a position direction from an unoriented galaxy axis
course_map.assessment_target: Separate a position direction from an unoriented galaxy axis

teaching_anchor.bridge_to_teach: Use x=(cos delta cos alpha,cos delta sin alpha,sin delta) for directed sky positions. An unoriented axis is the pair{x,-x}. Its angle uses arccos(abs(x dot y)); a directed angle does not take the absolute value. Read G04 pp1,3 and G02 p3 before identifying the observation domain.

worked_example.task_and_answer: RA0,Dec0 gives e_x; RA180,Dec0 gives-e_x. As directed sky positions their separation is180deg. As one projective axis their separation is0. G04 reports114381 unique directed positions and no radial distance inferred; the earlier galaxy-axis pathway is a different object.

guided_practice.task_and_answer: RA90,Dec0 gives e_y and has90deg directed and axial angle to e_x. G04 p3 uses antipodal completion within discovery operators, but final fitting/assignments use actual directed vectors. Retain the original direction when forming a projective discovery view.

diagnostic.task_and_answer: A direction does not specify radial distance or a galaxy intrinsic axis. Treating x and-x as the same observed position loses information; the source only grants that equivalence inside its declared discovery operators.

course_map.title: Spherical response and phase addresses
course_map.worked_example_capability: Trace a source-defined response into an address system
course_map.assessment_target: Trace a source-defined response into an address system

teaching_anchor.bridge_to_teach: Keep two source-local maps distinct. G03 is a historical Cell3 spherical-response construction with u=n dot N,kappa=nu*pi/(h*u),q=kappa n,loop phases,F,D and G_star=D/F. G04 p4 defines reciprocal plane addresses q_j dot x=k_j+phi_j. Matching variable letters do not identify these maps.

worked_example.task_and_answer: Synthetic response card: n=N=e_z,h=1L,nu=1 gives u=1,kappa=pi/L,q=(0,0,pi/L). With stipulated zero loop phases and nonnegative weights, F=sqrt(9)/3=1,D=0,G_star=0. Separately a reciprocal row(1,0)/L and x=(5/4,0)L give phase5/4, k=1,phi=1/4.

guided_practice.task_and_answer: C29-DOMAIN-D1: n=e_x,N=e_z gives u=0 and undefined first-lock kappa/q. A separately stipulated phase set all2pi/3 gives F=0; G_star=D/F is undefined even if D=0. Retain inputs and null plus the appropriate flag. In a regular synthetic transfer D=2,F=1/2, G_star=4 relative units.

diagnostic.task_and_answer: G03 absolute scalar gravity calibration is undefined and its precision is binary64 with separate null flags. It does not supply the galaxy direct basis or a calibrated force law. A response singularity is not a deleted direction.

course_map.worked_example_capability: Read its basis, units, handedness, and origin
course_map.assessment_target: Read its basis, units, handedness, and origin

teaching_anchor.bridge_to_teach: Read G01 basis/reciprocal/phase pointers and G02/G04 p4. A_gal has columns a,b,c; Q_gal has reciprocal columns, Q_gal^T A_gal=I. R_gal_rows=A_gal^-1=Q_gal^T differs from inverse Gram metric M_gal^-1. Centers are A_gal(k+phi), with phi dimensionless.

worked_example.task_and_answer: C29-PHASE-EX1: synthetic A=I2 L,phi=(1/4,1/2),k=(1,-1) gives center(5/4,-1/2)L and zero-index center Aphi=(1/4,1/2)L. Recover k=A^-1 center-phi. G01 has positive determinant, while mature Cell3 preserves its negative handedness.

guided_practice.task_and_answer: For synthetic A=diag(2,3)L with the same k,phi, center=(5/2,-3/2)L and zero-index center=(1/2,3/2)L. Reciprocal rows are(1/2,0)/L and(0,1/3)/L; inverse Gram metric is diag(1/4,1/9)/L^2. Identify every type and unit.

diagnostic.task_and_answer: Aphi is not phi. G02 unit-sphere reconstruction lengths have no radial physical calibration; do not divide them by Cell3 nm. Source stored Q^T A closure is retained at its decimal precision rather than rounded into literal equality.

course_map.title: Shared grammar and distinct metrics
course_map.worked_example_capability: Compare galaxy and Cell3 constructions without identifying their physical normals
course_map.assessment_target: Compare galaxy and Cell3 constructions without identifying their physical normals

teaching_anchor.bridge_to_teach: Shared transport grammar can be derived for different nonsingular ordered bases without equating their metrics or physical normals. For a,b,c define s_ab=(a-b)/2,s_ac=(a-c)/2,s_bc=(b-c)/2. Their closure s_ac=s_ab+s_bc is algebraic. The metric-dual sheet normal is proportional to A^-T(1,1,1).

worked_example.task_and_answer: For synthetic A=diag(1,2,3)L, s_ab=(1/2,-1,0)L,s_bc=(0,1,-3/2)L,s_ac=(1/2,0,-3/2)L. Their sum closes and N_unscaled=(1,1/2,1/3)/L is orthogonal to each root. A second basis diag(2,1,4)L has the same closure but different Gram metric.

guided_practice.task_and_answer: Compute the second roots(1,-1/2,0),(0,1/2,-2),(1,0,-2)L and verify closure. C29-TYPE-D1: a galaxy reconstruction-length/Cell3-nm quotient is not an admitted physical scale ratio without a galaxy radial calibration. G02 pp17–20 keeps metric anisotropy and ICRS orientation distinct despite common topology.

diagnostic.task_and_answer: The source projective sheet-normal difference28.574681962...deg and hard/soft ratios are attributed comparisons, not identical normals. Historical Cell3 ratios in G02 p7 cannot overwrite S02 mature locked values. Preserve numeric analogues as candidates, not forced algebra.

course_map.title: Distance metrics and ellipsoids
course_map.worked_example_capability: Reconstruct distance from a small positive metric
course_map.assessment_target: Reconstruct distance from a small positive metric

teaching_anchor.bridge_to_teach: For dimensionless address displacement q, define squared distance q^T M q with positive symmetric M in L^2. Teach inverse and cross term, then distinguish metric distance to a candidate center from componentwise rounding. A distance requires a nonnegative square root; an inverse metric has reciprocal units.

worked_example.task_and_answer: C29-MET-EX1: M=[[2,1],[1,2]]L^2 has leading minors2 and3 and inverse(1/3)[[2,-1],[-1,2]]L^-2. q=(1,-1) gives squared distance2L^2 and distance sqrt(2)L. Eigenvalues1,3 define ellipse axes1 and1/sqrt(3) for unit distance in normalized coordinates.

guided_practice.task_and_answer: C29-MET-P1 q=(1,1) gives6L^2, distance sqrt(6)L. C29-SKEW-P1: A columns(1,0),(0.9,0.1)L,phi=0,q=(0.49,0.49) gives x=(0.931,0.049)L. Rounded owner0 has squared distance0.869162L^2; center b has0.003562L^2. Rounding is not nearest-center assignment. This comparison does not certify a global closest center.

diagnostic.task_and_answer: C29-MET-D1: diag(1,-1) is not a positive distance metric since q=(0,1) gives-1. G04 p4 requires an explicit local closest-vector calculation with metric; a nearest-point proof needs a bounded candidate/completeness argument, not merely testing b.

course_map.title: Recursive occupancy and retained residuals
course_map.worked_example_capability: Track occupancy across levels without discarding sparse or weak regions
course_map.assessment_target: Track occupancy across levels without discarding sparse or weak regions

teaching_anchor.bridge_to_teach: Occupancy is a full count vector indexed by cell/state and depth; retain zeros and parent-child mappings. Separate combinatorial availability of27 nodes and seven sheets from observed galaxy counts. Each source assignment also retains vector, angular and radial residuals.

worked_example.task_and_answer: Enumerate(i,j,k) in{-1,0,1}^3 and sheet lambda=i+j+k: populations(1,3,6,7,6,3,1), total27. These are available nodes, not observed galaxy fractions. A synthetic parent with child counts(1,2,1) contains4 objects; preserve all three bins and the4 IDs.

guided_practice.task_and_answer: A synthetic held-out child vector(0,3,1) also totals4, with held-out minus discovery(-1,1,0). Keep the zero first bin. For an observed unit vector x=(1,0,0) and candidate center c=(4/5,0,0), vector residual=(1/5,0,0), Euclidean residual1/5, angular miss0 and radial mismatch-1/5. These answer different questions.

diagnostic.task_and_answer: Do not delete sparse bins or infer empirical occupancy from sheet combinatorics. At zero center c=0 its direction/angular miss is undefined; preserve the center and flag. No radial distance to the galaxy is supplied by the unit-shell mismatch.

course_map.worked_example_capability: Explain a frozen comparison and retain phase drifts and mismatches
course_map.assessment_target: Explain a frozen comparison and retain phase drifts and mismatches

teaching_anchor.bridge_to_teach: Read G04 p3:57076 discovery and57305 holdout positions. Discovery chooses normals, spacings, phases and triad; freeze them before holdout assignment. Keep phase drifts, every occupancy difference and source-defined controls. Descriptive source statistics do not authorize erasing mismatches.

worked_example.task_and_answer: 57076+57305=114381. G01 contains separate seven-sheet discovery, holdout and rotation-mean vectors. Report all seven held-out minus discovery differences using the verification ledger, not only their correlation. G02 pp17–20 distinguishes mixed branch-lift occupancy from pure sheet/A2 coordinate comparisons.

guided_practice.task_and_answer: For the toy occupancy vectors(1,2,1) and(0,3,1), report(-1,1,0), retaining all bins. Freeze phi=(1/4,1/2) for a toy holdout point; a suggested shift to(1/3,1/2) after inspecting it is a new exploratory fit. Keep the original assignment, changed assignment and phase difference(1/12,0), rather than replacing the frozen result.

diagnostic.task_and_answer: The reported discovery/holdout correlation0.999513500... does not remove any phase or occupancy discrepancy. G01 pure-coordinate source interpretation remains a separate result; quote its statistical language only as attributed reporting. Do not silently recast a reused holdout as independent discovery.

course_map.title: A cross-domain explanatory map
course_map.worked_example_capability: Compare recurring structures by explicit transformations and independent predictions
course_map.assessment_target: Compare recurring structures by explicit transformations and independent predictions

teaching_anchor.bridge_to_teach: Construct a cross-domain map with source roles, units, explicit coordinate transformations, invariants and candidate predictions. A common basis-derived identity is weaker than a physical correspondence; the distinction tells the next test which information is needed. Compare normalized quantities only under stated normalization.

worked_example.task_and_answer: For a uniform rescale A->2A, Gram M->4M, volume V->8V and root vectors->2roots. The normalized metric M/|det A|^(2/3) is invariant. An orientation change U with U^T U=I preserves Gram, while a change of shape generally does not. These are explicit synthetic comparisons.

guided_practice.task_and_answer: G02 p19 proposes hard-mode-aligned depletion as a future test, not a performed independent result. Freeze the source eigenframe, candidate state set, catalog inclusion rules and full-state occupancy transform before a new independent catalog. Retain every state, signed difference, angular/vector/radial residual, selection-function input and missing-distance field. A changed eigenframe is a separate exploratory branch.

diagnostic.task_and_answer: Candidate ratio analogues on G02 pp19–20 have multiplicity and source-calibration boundaries. An independent prediction must specify a frozen mapping, observable and falsifying pattern; it cannot merely restate a similarity after fitting the new data.

lessons.bridge_to_teach: Use x=(cos delta cos alpha,cos delta sin alpha,sin delta) for directed sky positions. An unoriented axis is the pair{x,-x}. Its angle uses arccos(abs(x dot y)); a directed angle does not take the absolute value. Read G04 pp1,3 and G02 p3 before identifying the observation domain.

worked_example.task_and_answer: RA0,Dec0 gives e_x; RA180,Dec0 gives-e_x. As directed sky positions their separation is180deg. As one projective axis their separation is0. G04 reports114381 unique directed positions and no radial distance inferred; the earlier galaxy-axis pathway is a different object.

guided_practice.task_and_answer: RA90,Dec0 gives e_y and has90deg directed and axial angle to e_x. G04 p3 uses antipodal completion within discovery operators, but final fitting/assignments use actual directed vectors. Retain the original direction when forming a projective discovery view.

diagnostic.task_and_answer: A direction does not specify radial distance or a galaxy intrinsic axis. Treating x and-x as the same observed position loses information; the source only grants that equivalence inside its declared discovery operators.

lessons.bridge_to_teach: Shared transport grammar can be derived for different nonsingular ordered bases without equating their metrics or physical normals. For a,b,c define s_ab=(a-b)/2,s_ac=(a-c)/2,s_bc=(b-c)/2. Their closure s_ac=s_ab+s_bc is algebraic. The metric-dual sheet normal is proportional to A^-T(1,1,1).

G02 pp17–20 keeps metric anisotropy and ICRS orientation distinct despite common topology.

An orientation change U with U^T U=I preserves Gram, while a change of shape generally does not. These are explicit synthetic comparisons.
